newsitem.title: GERMANY: BASF looks to sell PMMA business.
newsitem.headline: BASF looks to sell PMMA business.

text.p: German chemicals and drugs group BASF AG said on Wednesday it was planning to sell its unprofitable PMMA synthetics division as part of plans to focus more strongly on core activities.

"We are looking to sell this business very quickly," a BASF spokesman said, adding BASF was planning to concentrate on other activities, realising it was impossible to "become a global player in all activities."
The PMMA --polymethyl methacrylate plastics business is run by units in Germany and Spain and posted sales of 130 million marks last year but made no profits, he added.
The German and Spanish units together employ 340 workers.
BASF has contacted investment bank Wasserstein Perella & Co to conduct the sale, the spokesman said.
He added BASF would be looking to sell the business to a candidate who would "do everything possible to secure jobs".
PMMA is also known as acrylic glass which is used in the automotive, construction and sanitary industries for things like car light covers, furniture parts, showers and bathtubs.

BASF, which last year took steps to sell off a number of unprofitable units including tape maker BASF Magnetics, said it would concentrate on core operations in poystyrene, styrene copolymers, and engineering plastics.
The BASF spokesman said it was not possible to say how quickly a sale could be completed or whether any companies had already expressed interest in the business.
Share traders welcomed the news, turning BASF into one of the day's most actively-traded issues and sending it up two percent to 60.75 marks.
